facts.fact: The Ministry of Local Government says that under the new integrated civil registration system births and deaths in health facilities are registered and certified there and those in communities are registered at cell level; the text gives no date for the launch, so the document's publication date is used.

The Ministry of Local Government says registration is completed at the health facility or the cell, in a system that links the National Centralized and Integrated CRVS, the National Population Registry, the CRVS web and the health information system so that institutions receive the same data without multiple entries; no date is given, so the publication date is used.

The Ministry of Local Government gives no count of offices registering in the system: it says 1,100 data managers and health facility managers in all public and private hospitals were trained over two months and that training of 2,148 cell executive secretaries on the new system was being conducted; no date is given, so the publication date is used.

The Ministry of Local Government says the Government upgraded the CRVS system through the National Identification Agency, with the ministry and the agency training the new civil registrars; no date is given, so the publication date is used.
The Ministry of Local Government cites an adopted CRVS strategy for 2017-2022 that seeks 95% birth and 90% death registration and certification; the strategy's end year is used as the date.

The Ministry of Local Government announces the launch of the new integrated civil registration system, moving the civil registrar's powers from sector level to cells and health facilities under an amended Law 32/2016; the text carries no launch date and the publication date is used, though it speaks of 2025 targets as ahead and of a 2017-2022 strategy as in force.
